definition: Classifying pulmonary nodules in CT scans as benign or malignant — a core lung-cancer screening task.
details: Classifying pulmonary nodules in CT scans as benign or malignant — a core lung-cancer screening task.

explainer.lead: Lung nodule classification is the task of labelling pulmonary nodules in CT scans as benign or malignant. It matters as a core lung-cancer screening task.

tiers.eli5: It's a computer helping doctors decide whether a small spot in a lung scan is harmless or cancer.
tiers.practitioner: Used to support lung-cancer screening on CT scans by distinguishing benign from malignant nodules; the facts given do not detail model architectures or error trade-offs.
tiers.paperLevel: A binary classification task over CT-detected pulmonary nodules: benign versus malignant; performance depends on the screening population and data.

explainer.example: A CT scan shows a small nodule, and the classifier flags it as benign or malignant for review.
